Subject: Final-round panel convergence — Aaron Chen (Backend SWE) — score reconciliation & next steps

Hi all,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning to interview Aaron for Backend SWE. Quick recap attached: resume + the scorecard snapshot. I captured the highlights below to speed up reconciliation.

High-level notes:
- Strengths: strong API design and caching tradeoffs, clear ownership examples, shipping-in-small-increments mindset.
- Risks: limited exposure to multi-region DB failover patterns (system-design depth), some uncertainty on infra automation ownership.
- Culture add: demonstrated clear communication with PMs and SREs.

Action items I need from the panel:
1) Please put your final numeric score on the Greenhouse scorecard by EOD today (link below). If you want to change your earlier feedback, add a one-line reason.
2) If you have a hard no or a strong hire (weird divergence), reply all with your stance and one sentence of rationale.
3) If you want a 10–15 min calibration call to align, indicate availability — proposing 3:15–3:30pm PT today.

Tentative ask: If we converge (>=3/4 hire or hire-with-conditions), Lydia will schedule an offer call; if not, we’ll reconvene and decide next steps.

Attachments: [Attachment: Aaron_Chen_Resume.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: scorecard-aaron-chen-20261130.pdf (pdf)]

Neha —

Thanks for the recap. I updated the Greenhouse scorecard (see attached snapshot) — final overall: 7/10. Quick bullets:
- Design (7): liked the API-first approach, but follow-up on multi-region failover was surface-level.
- Coding (8): clean implementation, good tests.
- Ownership (7): solid examples, could name more infra automation work.

I don't have a hard no. Given hiring needs for Q1 and his ramp profile I lean hire-with-mentorship (L4). Happy to jump on the 3:15 sync if helpful.

D

I pulled my notes into GH as well — final overall: 5/10.
- Design (4): I’m concerned the design answers didn’t sufficiently account for cross-region leader election and live migrations; those are critical for the work we need.
- Coding (6): competent but not exceptional.
- Ownership (5): limited infra automation examples; may need strong mentoring to own services end-to-end.

Given the gap on multi-region resiliency, I’m leaning towards passing for this role at this level. If others strongly disagree, I’ll join a 15-min calibration to talk specifics.

Karthik
Principal SWE, Reliability Engineering

Thanks, Neha —

I went back and re-listened to the system-design portion. My final overall: 8/10.
- Design (8): I think Aaron actually surfaced a viable multi-region strategy when prompted — suggested active/passive with automated failover plus async replication for non-critical state. He didn’t lead with it but showed the right thought process when pushed.
- Coding (8): strong.
- Ownership (8): shows product-scope thinking and good cross-team communication examples.

I'm comfortable with a hire at L4, with a 3-month onboarding plan that pairs him with SRE for runbook/DR bootcamp. I can be the partner on that onboarding if we extend. I can make 3:15–3:30pm PT today.

Evelyn
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability

Karthik, I acknowledge your concern about leader-election depth — thank you for the callout. Evelyn and Dylan, thanks for specifying onboarding support.

- Karthik: if you'd like, we can do a 15-min calibration tomorrow to walk the exact technical expectations before offer goes out; let me know a time.

Lydia, copying Aaron here to confirm next steps — Aaron, congrats from the interview panel. Lydia will reach out with an offer call time tomorrow. If you have any constraints, please reply-all with your availability.
